text:
Diego (Design): Quick sync on the catalog UI tweaks: trying to reduce visual clutter while keeping variant detail discoverable. Main pain points: performance badges dominate rows, legend takes up too much vertical space, and users are unclear when a pinned version is actually the one compared. Any quick wins? Ava (PM): From support logs users ask 'which version is in the comparison?' frequently. Can we add a persistent row-level affordance that reads "Comparing: v2-quant" instead of just an icon? Also prefer explicit words over icon-only labels. Sam (Frontend): Concur. Current layout uses small chips that collapse on narrow screens which makes identity ambiguous. Suggestion: compact badge with icon + 2-char label for table then full label in tooltip/focus. Also implement focus-visible outlines for badges. Marta (A11y): Important: badges must not rely on color alone. Add text alternative inside badge (sr-only) and ensure tooltip content is reachable via keyboard. Proposed aria pattern: put badge in a button with aria-expanded for the popover and focusable. Eg: ```
p50=28ms p95=110ms est $0.0018/token
``` Priya (Eng-ML): On pin persistence: frontend-only pin is causing mismatch during refresh. Backend should accept a body like { pinned_variant_id: "v2-quant" } and persist per-account. Edge-case: when a pinned variant is deprecated, return pinned_variant_status: "missing" and provide fallback suggestions. Nina (Research): In user interviews ppl described badges as "badges screaming" lol. We tested a condensed legend with microcopy and users liked a short line: "Performance: latency · cost · model quality (hover for numbers)". That seemed to reduce confusion. Diego (Design): Nice quote :) For the legend UI, what if we hide the legend by default and show a tiny help icon that expands inline? Keeps real estate but keeps discoverability. Ava (PM): That could work. Add telemetry on expand so we can see if people need it. Also change CTA copy from "Lock" to "Pin version to compare" per previous tests. Sam (Frontend): I'll mock a CSS pattern to collapse/expand legend and provide keyboard toggles. Will add telemetry events: legend_toggled, badge_tooltip_opened, pin_saved. DeployBot: Staging link updated: https://staging.redwood.ai/catalog?ui=compact-legend -- partial rollout. Marta (A11y): Also recommend live announcements when pin state changes: `aria-live="assertive"` message like "Pinned v2-quant for comparison" to help screen reader users. And ensure undo toast is keyboard dismissible. Priya (Eng-ML): Backend note: we should include a /catalog/:model_id?include_pinned=true param so older clients still work. And log pin changes for audit. There's also a cache-implication for Dedicated customers: pinned variants should pin caching hints; I'll write a short migration plan. Diego (Design): UX detail: when a user pins a variant from the compare modal, the modal should show a small confirmation line: "Will pin v2-quant across your workspace until you unpin. Undo?" with a quick undo button. Nina (Research): Also flagging that some users want per-project pinning vs global account pinning. Needs product decision — I'll add notes from interviews. Ava (PM): Let's track that as an open question. For now scope to account-level pinning. Acceptance criteria for ticket: compact legend toggle, accessible tooltip, pinned_variant persisted server-side, undo toast, telemetry. Sam (Frontend): I'll attach a tiny prototype and keyboard screenshots in the ticket. ETA: PR in 6 days. Priya (Eng-ML): I'll draft the API contract and migration notes, and include error handling for missing variants. Diego (Design): Thanks team. I'll push mocks and copy variations into the shared Figma link tomorrow and leave examples of confusing support transcripts here for context. Ava (PM): I'll open the product issue and add the checklist. Marta (A11y): Quick reminder: include checklist items for keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements. Sam (Frontend): Got it, will include tests. :rocket:
